samples.xml_description:
<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Implement a series-parallel conversion circuit. It receives a serial input signal "din_serial" along with a control signal "din_valid" indicating the validity of the input data. The module operates on the rising edge of the clock signal "clk" and uses a synchronous design. The input din_serial is a single-bit data, and when the module receives 8 input data, the output dout_parallel outputs the 8-bit data(The serial input values are sequentially placed in dout_parallel from the most significant bit to the least significant bit), and the dout_valid is set to 1.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="MAX_COUNT" value="4'd8">Maximum count value for the counter.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[3:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of serial inputs received.</reg>
        <reg id="valid_reg">Register to store the validity signal for the output data.</reg>
        <always_comb>
            if (din_valid && cnt == MAX_COUNT) begin
                cnt <= 4'b0;
                valid_reg <= 1'b1;
            end else if (din_valid) begin
                cnt <= cnt + 1;
                valid_reg <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                cnt <= cnt;
                valid_reg <= 1'b0;
            end
        </always_comb>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Use a counter to keep track of the number of serial inputs received. When all 8 serial data bits have been received, set the valid output signal to 1. Otherwise, set the valid output signal to 0.</implementation>
</module>
